title: Renewal readiness - operational metric recipes and QBR KPI slate
body:
Purpose

This is a working template for Customer Success QBRs focused on renewal-readiness: concise metric definitions + reproducible measurement recipes for the four most important signals we use during renewal conversations — latency, availability (uptime), cost-per-token, and cache hit rate — plus a compact KPI slate and a short action playbook.

Audience
- CSMs preparing renewal QBR decks
- Solutions Engineers who validate data and recommend mitigations
- Customer Success leadership who want consistent scoring across accounts

Notes-to-self: keep the room-level math explicit so AE/CS can reproduce numbers during exec calls. Include SQL/PromQL examples and the exact Redwood Console metric names.

Metric definitions and measurement recipes
1) 95th percentile request latency (ms) - definition
- What we report: p95 of server-side response time for text/generation/chat endpoints, measured at token-stream finalization (end-to-end server processing, excludes network tail if instrumentation supports it).
- Why it matters: higher p95 correlates with bad UX and higher abandonment at scale.
- Measurement window: rolling 30 days (default for QBR slice), also include 7d and 90d for trend context.
- Data sources: Redwood Console -> metrics -> request_latency_ms.p95 (per-route), ingested into monitoring db.
- Recipe (pseudo-SQL):
  SELECT
    route,
    percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) AS p95_latency_ms,
    count(*) AS requests
  FROM request_latency_events
  WHERE created_at BETWEEN '{{window_start}}' AND '{{window_end}}'
  GROUP BY route;
- PromQL (if using Prometheus ingestion):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[30d])) by (le, route)) * 1000
- Reporting notes: exclude synthetic health-check endpoints and internal tooling routes. Flag large request counts from tooling loads (CS demo traffic).

2) Uptime / Availability - definition
- What we report: percentage of successful responses (2xx/3xx) vs total API attempts, computed per-month and for the quarter. If a customer has Dedicated or Private deployment, include SLA window and scheduled maintenance separately.
- Measurement window: month-to-date and trailing 90 days for QBR.
- Data sources: Redwood Console -> request_status_counts, billing logs for scheduled maint windows.
- Recipe (pseudo-SQL):
  SELECT
    1.0 - (SUM(case when status_code >= 500 then 1 else 0 end)::float / SUM(1)::float) AS availability
  FROM request_status_events
  WHERE created_at BETWEEN '{{window_start}}' AND '{{window_end}}';
- Edge cases: 429 throttles should be reported separately (throttling indicates quota issues not service outages).
- SLA note: For Dedicated/Private customers, compute availability RESTATING: availability = uptime_excluding_scheduled / total_time_excluding_scheduled.

3) Cost per token (USD) - definition
- What we report: aggregated cost to Redwood (or committed unit pricing proxy) divided by billed tokens for the period; shown as cents per token (or $/1k tokens). We prefer $/1k tokens for readability.
- Why it matters: cost drift drives renewal price discussions.
- Data sources: billing_events (raw GPU-hours, quantization profile, model variant), token_counter (per-request token_consumed).
- Recipe (pseudo-SQL):
  SELECT
    SUM(cost_usd) / NULLIF(SUM(tokens), 0) * 1000 AS usd_per_1k_tokens
  FROM (
    SELECT request_id, tokens_consumed AS tokens, model_cost_usd(request_id) AS cost_usd
    FROM request_billing
    WHERE created_at BETWEEN '{{window_start}}' AND '{{window_end}}'
  );
- Practical simplification: if exact model_cost_usd is unavailable, use committed cost-per-GPU-hour * GPU-hours attributable to the customer. Document assumptions.
- Include note: separate out high-latency/cold-start requests since they distort cost-per-token if they trigger extra work.

4) Cache hit rate (prefix/KV cache) - definition
- What we report: fraction of requests where we served prefix or KV cache that avoided re-computation (i.e., served from cached KV/embeds or cached prefix). Shown as percentage and absolute saved token-count estimate.
- Data sources: cache_events (hit/miss), kv_cache_logs, prefix_cache_metrics.
- Recipe (pseudo-SQL):
  SELECT
    SUM(case when event_type = 'hit' then 1 else 0 end)::float / SUM(1)::float AS cache_hit_rate
  FROM cache_events
  WHERE created_at BETWEEN '{{window_start}}' AND '{{window_end}}' AND cache_namespace = '{{customer_ns}}';
- Token savings estimate: estimate_saved_tokens = SUM(tokens_skipped_on_hit). If not tracked precisely, approximate by average tokens_per_request * hits.
- Reporting caveat: large embed-only workloads can show near-zero prefix hits but high embed reuse; include separate embedding-reuse metric if important.

KPI Slate (Compact table to paste into QBR slide)
- Format: Metric | Window | Current | Change (vs prev) | Target | Notes
- Example for fictitious account "AcmeSearch" (last quarter vs previous quarter):
  Metric | Window | Current | Change | Target | Notes
  p95 latency (ms) | 30d | 370 | +22% | <250 | p95 spike on 2026-02-10 due to model rollout
  Availability (%) | 90d | 99.93 | -0.04pp | >=99.95 | two 5-min incidents (fallbacks worked)
  Cost per 1k tokens (USD) | 30d | 2.40 | +12% | <=1.80 | usage shifted to long-context model variant
  Cache hit rate (%) | 30d | 28 | +6pp | >=45 | prefix cache tuning needed, embedding reuse steady

Metric scoring (simple renewal-ready index)
- We propose a lightweight score (0-100) to assist renewal priority. Each metric maps to 0-25 points then summed:
  p95 latency (0-25): <=200ms=25, 200-350=15, >350=5
  Availability (0-25): >=99.95=25, 99.9-99.95=15, <99.9=5
  Cost per 1k tokens (0-25): <=1.5=25, 1.5-2.5=15, >2.5=5
  Cache hit rate (0-25): >=45=25, 25-45=15, <25=5
- Example AcmeSearch: p95=5, availability=15, cost=15, cache=15 => total 50/100. Red flag if score <=60.

Short action playbook (during QBR and 60-day renewal window)
- If score <=60 (renewal risk):
  1) Convene SE + infra owner to run the "fast mitigation" checklist within 7 days:
     - Rollback model variant if rollout correlated to p95 increase
     - Apply temporary cache bypass policy for heavy tail requests (to avoid cascade)
     - Increase dedicated burst capacity for peak windows (if Dedicated) or enable region fallback
  2) Cost interventions:
     - Suggest batching and token-trim prompts for high-volume routes
     - Recommend quantized variant for non-critical routes; provide estimated cost savings (link to Optimize suggestions)
  3) Cache interventions:
     - Update prefix cache TTL and warm top-50 prefixes prior to peak
     - Deploy a lightweight cached-response layer for identical queries (SE/Dev team task)
- If score >60 (healthy):
  - Document small improvements and schedule a mid-quarter check-in. Confirm roadmap items that could affect metrics (model upgrade, new features).

Owners & responsibilities
- CSM: assemble KPI slate, narrative, and customer-facing asks. 
- SE: validate the data sources and execute the technical mitigations.
- Infra/SRE: investigate root cause for availability and latency incidents.
- Finance/RevOps: validate cost-assumptions in the cost-per-token calculation.

Appendix: quick debug queries and checks (notes)
- Check model variant rollouts: SELECT variant, count(*) FROM request_model_variants WHERE ts BETWEEN ... GROUP BY variant;
- Look for correlated spikes: join p95 timeline with deployment events and autoscaler logs.
- Verify quotas: get 429 counts per route (429s often precede SLA complaints).

Open questions / TODOs
- We still need a standard method to attribute GPU-hours to Hosted customers at the per-customer level; file a ticket (CS-482) for Finance and Infra to agree on a canonical mapping.
- Decide whether to include 50th percentile latency or mean latency in the public KPI slate (p95 preferred for safety).
- Add a small section on embeddings reuse metric if customer uses embeddings heavily.

Draft status and next steps
- Drafted by Maya 2025-11-03. Reviewed by Diego and Priya 2025-11-18.
- Action: SEs to validate SQL/PromQL snippets against production telemetry. Target to finalize template for board QBRs by 2026-03-15.

Contact
